details.content: Enteric (Typhoid/Paratyphoid) fever (fever, rose spots, splenomegaly, leukopenia, intestinal hemorrhage/perforation in 3rd week), gastroenteritis, septicemia.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Widal test for auxiliary diagnosis. Antibiotics (ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin). Typhoid vaccine (Vi polysaccharide) available.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: G- comma-shaped curved rod, single polar flagellum ("shuttling like fish" darting motility).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Facultative anaerobe; grows in highly alkaline media (pH 8.5-9.5, alkaline peptone water); yellow colonies on TCBS agar.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Very weak; sensitive to heat, drying, and gastric acid; killed at 100°C in 2 minutes.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Flagella (penetrates mucus), pili (TCP, attachment), Cholera Toxin (exotoxin, activates adenylate cyclase -> high cAMP -> hypersecretion of water/electrolytes).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Cholera (severe, painless watery diarrhea, "rice-water" stools, extreme dehydration, muscle cramps, hypovolemic shock).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Immediate, massive oral/IV rehydration (essential), tetracycline/doxycycline to shorten shedding. Quarantine, sanitation.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: G- polymorphic curved rod, halophilic (requires high salt, 3.5% NaCl).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Halophilic growth, green colonies on TCBS, Kanagawa phenomenon positive (produces thermostable direct hemolysin).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, acid, and fresh water (dies in tap water).

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Thermostable direct hemolysin (TDH) and TDH-related hemolysin (TRH) (cytotoxic, cardiotoxic).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Food poisoning (acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, fever) associated with raw/undercooked seafood.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Self-limiting; hydration. Antibiotics only for severe cases.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: G+ slender bacilli with terminal round spores, presenting a characteristic "drum-stick" appearance.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Obligate anaerobe, difficult to grow, swarming growth on blood agar.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Spores are extremely resistant; survive boiling for hours; killed only by autoclaving at 121°C under pressure.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Tetanospasmin (powerful neurotoxin, blocks release of inhibitory neurotransmitters GABA/glycine -> continuous muscle contraction).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Tetanus (lockjaw, trismus, spastic paralysis, opisthotonus, facial grimace/risus sardonicus). Wound must be anaerobic (deep/dirty).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Wound debridement, Tetanus Antitoxin (TAT, must perform skin test first!), penicillin/metronidazole, DPT toxoid vaccine for prevention.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: G+ large rectangular bacilli, non-motile, forms capsule in vivo, subterminal oval spore.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Anaerobic; produces "stormy fermentation" in milk medium (clots and gas) and double-zone hemolysis on blood agar.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Spores are highly resistant to heat, drying, and chemical disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Alpha toxin (lecithinase, damages cell membranes, causes tissue necrosis and hemolysis), enterotoxin, theta toxin.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Gas gangrene (myonecrosis, gas bubbles in tissue, foul odor, high mortality), food poisoning (watery diarrhea from reheated meat).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Surgical debridement, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, high-dose penicillin G, gas gangrene polyvalent antitoxin.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: G+ bacilli, peritrichous flagella, subterminal oval spores ("tennis racket" shape).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Obligate anaerobe, grows on blood agar or cooked meat medium.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Spores are extremely heat-resistant. However, the botulinum neurotoxin itself is heat-labile (destroyed by boiling for 10 min).

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Botulinum neurotoxin (the most potent poison known; blocks acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junctions -> flaccid paralysis).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Botulism (foodborne from canned foods: double vision, dysphagia, descending flaccid paralysis, respiratory failure). Infant botulism.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Trivalent botulinum antitoxin, intensive respiratory support. Heat canned food thoroughly before consumption.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Acid-fast positive thin, straight rods, waxy lipid-rich cell wall (mycolic acid), non-spore, non-motile.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Obligate aerobe; grows extremely slowly (doubling time 18 hrs); rough, wrinkled, off-white "bread crumb" colonies on Löwenstein-Jensen (L-J) medium in 2-4 weeks.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: High resistance to drying, acids, and alkalis (survives 3% HCl / 4% NaOH for 15 min); sensitive to wet heat (65°C 15min), alcohol (75%), and UV.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Intracellular survival in macrophages, lipids (cord factor, wax D, sulfatide, phospholipid) cause tissue necrosis and granuloma.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Tuberculosis: Primary TB (tubercles, caseous necrosis), Post-primary TB (secondary reactivation, lung cavities, chronic cough, bloody sputum), Miliary TB (disseminated).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Tuberculin skin test (PPD/OT) for diagnosis. BCG vaccine (live attenuated M. bovis) for infants. Multi-drug therapy (Isoniazid, Rifampin, Streptomycin).

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Acid-fast positive rods, typically arranged in bundles (globi) inside histiocytes.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cannot be cultivated on artificial media or cell culture. Can only grow in armadillos or footpads of mice.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Similar to M. tuberculosis (highly resistant to environmental factors).

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Infection of skin histiocytes and Schwann cells of peripheral nerves, leading to demyelination and nerve damage.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Leprosy (Hansen's disease): Lepromatous leprosy (severe, nodular skin lesions, lion-like facies) or Tuberculoid leprosy (local anesthetic skin macules).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Multi-drug therapy: Dapsone, Rifampin, and Clofazimine. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Pleomorphic, small, completely lacks a peptidoglycan cell wall; bounded by a triple-layered sterol membrane.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Enriched agar containing sterols/serum; grows slowly (takes 2-3 weeks), forming tiny "fried egg" colonies.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly sensitive to drying, heat, osmotic shock, and antibiotics targeting cell wall (completely resistant to penicillin/beta-lactams).

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: P1 adhesin (attaches to respiratory cilia, inhibits ciliary action), hydrogen peroxide production.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Primary Atypical Pneumonia (PAP, walking pneumonia: dry hacking cough, fever, headache, patchy infiltrates on X-ray). Cold agglutination test positive.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Macrolides (erythromycin, azithromycin) or tetracycline/doxycycline. Resistant to beta-lactams.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Small, obligate intracellular bacteria. Exists in two forms: Elementary Body (EB, small, infectious, extracellular) and Reticulate Body (RB, large, replicative, intracellular).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Requires living host cells (yolk sac of embryonated eggs, McCoy cell cultures). Forms glycogen-containing inclusion bodies.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, lipid solvents, and antibiotics.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Intracellular replication cycle (EB -> RB -> binary fission -> EB -> cell lysis). Direct cellular damage and chronic inflammation.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Trachoma (serotypes A-C, chronic conjunctivitis, blindness), inclusion conjunctivitis, nongonococcal urethritis (NGU), Lymphogranuloma Venereum (LGV, serotypes L1-L3).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Tetracycline/doxycycline, erythromycin, or azithromycin.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Small, pleomorphic Gram-negative coccobacilli, visible under light microscope.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Obligate intracellular parasite; cultivated in yolk sacs of embryonated eggs, tissue culture, or susceptible animals (guinea pigs).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, drying, disinfectants, and antibiotics.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Endothelial cell infection, multiplying in cytoplasm -> vasculitis, thrombosis, rash. Weil-Felix reaction (cross-reacts with Proteus OX19).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Epidemic typhus (severe fever, headache, macular rash, stupor/delirium). Transmitted by the human body louse.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Vector control (louse control). Tetracyclines (doxycycline) or chloramphenicol. Live vaccine strain E used experimentally.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Thin, spiral-shaped with close, regular spirals; Gram-negative but stained by Fontana silver stain (brown); dark-field microscopy for live motility.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cannot be cultivated on artificial media. Can be maintained in rabbit epithelial cells but grows very slowly.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Very weak; sensitive to heat, drying, oxygen, soap, and standard disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Hyaluronidase, outer membrane proteins. Damages endothelial cells of blood vessels, leading to endarteritis.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Syphilis: Primary (painless chancre), Secondary (diffuse skin rash, condylomata lata), Tertiary (gummas, cardiovascular/neurosyphilis). Congenital syphilis.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Penicillin G is highly effective and remains the first choice. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Tightly coiled spirals with hook-shaped ends, forming characteristic "C" or "S" shapes. Gram-negative; stained by Fontana silver stain.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Aerobic; can be cultivated in liquid media containing animal serum (Korthof medium); grows slowly at 28-30°C.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly sensitive to drying and acid; can survive in neutral/alkaline water for weeks.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Invasion through broken skin/mucosa from water contaminated with infected rodent/domestic animal urine.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Leptospirosis (zoonosis, common in farmers): biphasic illness with fever, muscle pain (especially calves), conjunctival suffusion, Weil's disease (jaundice, renal failure).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Penicillin G or doxycycline. Rodent control, vaccination of domestic animals, avoid contaminated water.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Large, loose spirals with wider distances than T. pallidum. Gram-negative; stained by silver impregnation.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Microaerophilic; cultivated in BSK (Barbour-Stoenner-Kelly) medium; grows slowly.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, drying, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmission via Ixodes tick bite. Outer surface proteins (Osp) trigger inflammatory response.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Lyme disease: Stage 1 (erythema migrans/bull's-eye rash), Stage 2 (carditis, neurological symptoms), Stage 3 (chronic arthritis).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Doxycycline or amoxicillin. Tick control, personal protection in endemic areas.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical or pleomorphic; genome consists of 8 segments of negative-sense ssRNA. Glycoprotein spikes: Hemagglutinin (HA) & Neuraminidase (NA).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in amniotic or allantoic cavities of embryonated chicken eggs or MDCK cell lines.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Enveloped; sensitive to lipid solvents (ether, alcohol), heat, acid, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: HA binds to sialic acid receptors on respiratory epithelium. NA liquefies mucus and aids viral release. Antigenic drift (epidemics) & shift (reassortment -> pandemics).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Influenza (flu): abrupt onset of high fever, muscle ache, headache, cough, sore throat. Risk of primary/secondary bacterial pneumonia.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Inactivated or live-attenuated vaccines. Neuraminidase inhibitors (Oseltamivir/Tamiflu) or M2 inhibitors (Amantadine).

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, paramyxovirus; non-segmented negative-sense ssRNA.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell culture; causes multinucleated giant cell formation (syncytia) and cytopathic effects (inclusion bodies).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Enveloped; highly sensitive to heat, acid, lipid solvents, and UV light.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmission via respiratory droplets. Virulence proteins cause fusion of infected cells. Mutated defective interfering particles (DIP) persist in brain.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Measles (rubeola): fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik's spots (white spots on buccal mucosa, diagnostic), maculopapular rash. Late complication: SSPE.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Live attenuated measles vaccine (part of MMR, given at 8 months and 7 years). Immunoglobulin for passive protection.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, paramyxovirus; negative-sense ssRNA. Only one antigenic type.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell culture or embryonated eggs.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, lipid solvents, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Respiratory droplet transmission. Disseminates from respiratory tract to salivary glands and other organs.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Mumps: painful swelling of one or both parotid salivary glands, fever. Complications include orchitis (can lead to infertility in males) and aseptic meningitis.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Live attenuated mumps vaccine (MMR vaccine). Lifetime immunity follows natural infection.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, togavirus; positive-sense ssRNA. One serotype.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell lines; displays poor cytopathic effects.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, organic solvents, and low pH.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Respiratory droplet transmission. Crosses the placenta (vertical transmission) to infect the fetus, halting mitosis and causing congenital defects.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Rubella (German measles): mild rash, fever, lymphadenopathy. Congenital Rubella Syndrome (CRS): cataracts, patent ductus arteriosus, deafness, microcephaly.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Live attenuated rubella vaccine (MMR vaccine). Women should not be vaccinated during pregnancy.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, paramyxovirus; negative-sense ssRNA. Lacks HA and NA.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Grows in cell culture; characteristically induces fusion of cells to form large multinucleated syncytia (giant cells).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly unstable in environment; sensitive to heat, acid, and detergents.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmission via droplets or contact. Infects bronchiolar epithelium, causing necrosis and plug formation of mucus/fibrin.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Bronchiolitis and bronchopneumonia in infants (most important cause of infant respiratory tract illness, 50-90% of bronchiolitis). Common cold in adults.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Supportive (oxygen, hydration). Ribavirin aerosol for severe cases. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Naked, small, icosahedral; positive-sense ssRNA. Three serotypes (1, 2, and 3).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Grows rapidly in primate cell cultures with clear cytopathic effects.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Naked capsid; highly resistant to lipid solvents (ether), acid (survives gastric acid), and detergents; sensitive to heat and chlorine.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Fecal-oral transmission. Replicates in pharynx/gut lymphoid tissue -> twice viremia -> invades CNS -> destroys motor neurons in spinal cord anterior horns.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Poliomyelitis (infantile paralysis): 90-95% inapparent/subclinical. Minor illness (fever, sore throat). Paralytic poliomyelitis (flaccid paralysis, muscle atrophy).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Sabin oral vaccine (OPV: live-attenuated, mucosal IgA + serum IgG, risk of reversion) or Salk vaccine (IPV: inactivated, serum IgG only, no reversion).

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Naked, small, icosahedral, enterovirus; positive-sense ssRNA.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell culture or newborn mice.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Resistant to ether, acid, and detergents.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Fecal-oral transmission. Group A targets skin/mucosa; Group B has tissue tropism for heart, pancreas, and meninges.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Group A: Herpangina, Hand-Foot-and-Mouth Disease, aseptic meningitis. Group B: viral myocarditis, pericarditis, Bornholm disease (pleurodynia).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Symptomatic treatment. Hand hygiene, sanitation.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Naked, double-shelled capsid resembling a wheel ("Rota"); segmented dsRNA (11 segments).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Difficult to cultivate in standard cell culture; requires trypsin pretreatment.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Relatively stable in environment; resistant to ether, acid, and mild heat.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Fecal-oral route. Infects and damages mature enterocytes in the duodenum and jejunum, leading to malabsorption of water and sodium.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Severe infantile diarrhea (leading cause of diarrheal hospitalizations in infants and young children worldwide; watery stools, vomiting, fever).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Oral or IV rehydration (critical). Rotavirus live-attenuated oral vaccines are available.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Naked, icosahedral picornavirus; positive-sense ssRNA. One serotype.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Grows slowly in cell culture without cytopathic effects.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Stable to acid (pH 3), ether, heat (60°C for 1 hr); inactivated by chlorine, formaldehyde, or boiling.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Fecal-oral transmission. Replicates in hepatocytes, immune-mediated destruction of infected cells causes liver damage.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Acute hepatitis A: fever, anorexia, nausea, jaundice. Almost always self-limiting, no chronic carrier state, not linked to liver cancer.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Symptomatic. Inactivated HAV vaccine for active immunization. Immune globulin for passive post-exposure prophylaxis.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, double-shelled spherical particle ("Dane particle", intact HBV), circular partially dsDNA. Serum contains small spherical & tubular HBsAg particles.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cannot be cultivated in cell lines. Chimpanzees are highly susceptible.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly stable; resists drying, freezing, and mild heat; inactivated by autoclaving or 100°C for 10 min.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmitted via blood, sex, or maternal-fetal (vertical). Uses reverse transcriptase for replication. Immune-mediated (CTLs) lysis of hepatocytes causes pathology.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Hepatitis B (acute and chronic). High risk of chronic carriage, cirrhosis, and primary hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Recombinant HBsAg vaccine. Post-exposure HBIG (passive). Antivirals (Tenofovir, Entecavir, interferon-alpha) for chronic infection.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, flavivirus; positive-sense ssRNA. Highly variable hypervariable regions.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Highly difficult to cultivate in vitro.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Enveloped; sensitive to heat, lipid solvents, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmitted primarily by blood transfusion, IV drug use. High rate of antigenic mutation leads to immune escape and persistent chronic infection.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Hepatitis C: acute infection is often subclinical, but >80% progresses to chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and liver cancer.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Direct-Acting Antivirals (DAAs, e.g., Sofosbuvir, Ledipasvir) offer a cure rate >95%. No vaccine due to high mutation.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Defective virus; spherical, contains negative-sense circular ssRNA, but uses HBV's envelope (HBsAg) for its outer coat.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Requires co-infection with HBV to replicate.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to detergents, heat, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmitted via blood or sex. Co-infection (simultaneous HBV/HDV) or Superinfection (HDV infects chronic HBV carrier; causes severe acute flare).

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Severe hepatitis, fulminant hepatitis, rapid progression to cirrhosis.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Prevented by HBV vaccination. Interferon-alpha is used with limited efficacy.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Naked, icosahedral, hepevirus; positive-sense ssRNA.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Grows poorly in cell culture.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Relatively stable; sensitive to high temperature and chlorine.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Fecal-oral transmission (often waterborne epidemics). Direct cytotoxicity or immune-mediated liver damage.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Acute hepatitis E: similar to HAV. No chronic state. Highly severe in pregnant women (mortality rate up to 20% in 3rd trimester).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Symptomatic support. Vaccine developed and used in some endemic countries.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, icosahedral capsid, linear dsDNA. Glycoprotein spikes.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Grows rapidly in many cell lines, causing cytopathic effects (cell swelling, giant cells, intranuclear inclusions).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, detergents, lipid solvents, and acid.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Direct contact transmission. Primary lytic infection in epithelial cells, then establishes latent infection in neurons of the trigeminal ganglia.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Herpes labialis (fever blisters, cold sores), gingivostomatitis, keratoconjunctivitis, sporadic herpes encephalitis (high mortality).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Acyclovir (inhibits viral DNA polymerase), Ganciclovir. Avoid direct contact during active lesions. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, linear dsDNA, structurally similar to HSV-1.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell culture; cytopathology identical to HSV-1.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, ether, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Sexual contact transmission or vertical neonatal transmission during delivery. Establishes latency in sacral nerve ganglia.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Genital herpes (painful vesicular lesions on genitalia, fever, inguinal lymphadenopathy), neonatal herpes (severe, systemic, high mortality).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Acyclovir, Famciclovir, Valacyclovir. Cesarean section if active lesions are present in the birth canal.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, icosahedral capsid, linear dsDNA. Structurally identical to other herpesviruses.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in human diploid cell cultures; grows slowly.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly unstable in environment; sensitive to heat, detergents, and drying.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Respiratory droplet transmission. Primary infection in respiratory tract, disseminates via blood to skin. Establishes latency in dorsal root sensory ganglia.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Chickenpox (varicella: pruritic vesicular rash appearing in waves, mostly in children). Shingles (herpes zoster: painful vesicular eruption along a dermatome, reactivating in elderly/immunosuppressed).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Acyclovir for shingles. Live-attenuated varicella vaccine (prevention). VZV immunoglobulin for exposed immunocompromised individuals.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, largest herpesvirus, linear dsDNA. Glycoprotein spikes.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Grows extremely slowly, only in human fibroblasts; characteristically produces cytomegaly (huge swollen cells with "owl's eye" intranuclear inclusions).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly sensitive to freezing, heat, and detergents.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmitted by blood, saliva, breast milk, semen, and placenta. Establishes latency in kidneys, salivary glands, and monocytes.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Congenital cytomegalic inclusion disease (microcephaly, calcifications, hepatosplenomegaly), cytomegalic mononucleosis (heterophile-negative), severe pneumonia/retinitis in AIDS.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Ganciclovir, Foscarnet. Screen blood products. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, icosahedral capsid, linear dsDNA. Outer envelope contains gp340/220.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cannot grow in standard cell lines; infects and immortalizes human B lymphocytes in vitro (uses CD21 receptor).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, ether, and standard disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Transmitted via saliva ("kissing disease"). gp120/gp340 binds CD21 on B cells. Immortalizes B cells, leading to uncontrolled proliferation.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Infectious mononucleosis (fever, sore throat, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytes), Burkitt's lymphoma (endemic in Africa), Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC, highly prevalent in Southern China).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Symptomatic. Acyclovir has no clinical benefit for acute mononucleosis. IgA anti-VCA antibody used to screen/monitor NPC. Subunit gp340 vaccine under development.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, diploid +ssRNA (two identical copies of positive RNA). Core contains reverse transcriptase, integrase, protease, and p24. gp120 & gp41 spikes.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in CD4+ T-lymphocyte cell lines or human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs).

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Enveloped; sensitive to heating (56°C 30min), lipid solvents, and 70% alcohol.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: gp120 binds to CD4 receptors and co-receptors (CCR5/CXCR4) on Helper T (Th) cells and macrophages. Reverse transcriptase copies RNA to dsDNA, which integrates into host genome. CTLs destroy infected Th cells -> collapse of cellular immunity.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS): long incubation; presenting with fever, lymphadenopathy, weight loss, followed by fatal opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis, Cryptococcus) and malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Combination Antiretroviral Therapy (ART/HAART: reverse transcriptase, protease, and integrase inhibitors). Safe sex, needle hygiene. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, bullet-shaped virus, negative-sense ssRNA. Glycoprotein spikes.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell culture (duck embryo or diploid cell lines) or mouse brain.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to lipid solvents, heat (56°C 1 hr), acid, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Bite of infected animal (saliva). Virus replicates locally in muscle, then ascends sensory nerves to spinal cord and brain. Form eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions (Negri bodies) in neurons.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Rabies: hydrophobia (spasms of swallowing muscles triggered by sight of water), hyper-salivation, agitation, seizures, progressive paralysis, 100% fatal encephalitis once symptoms begin.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Immediate wound washing with soap & water, passive immunization (Rabies Immunoglobulin, HRIG) around wound, active immunization (killed rabies vaccine, HDCV).

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, bunyavirus; segmented negative-sense ssRNA (3 segments: L, M, S).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in Vero cells or suckling mice.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, acid, detergents, and organic solvents.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Natural host: striped field mouse (*Apodemus agrarius*). Shed in mouse urine, feces, saliva. Inhaled as aerosols -> infects vascular endothelial cells -> capillary leakage.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS): fever, hemorrhage, hypotension/shock, oliguria, anuria, renal failure. Typical "three-red" (flushed face, neck, chest).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Supportive fluid management. Ribavirin (reduces mortality if given early). Rodent control is the primary prevention.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, flavivirus; positive-sense ssRNA.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in cell lines or suckling mouse brain.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, ether, acid, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Vector: Culex tritaeniorhynchus mosquito. Reservoir hosts: pigs and birds. Mosquito bite -> viremia -> crosses blood-brain barrier -> infects CNS neurons.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Japanese B Encephalitis: high fever, headache, vomiting, meningeal signs, altered mental status, stupor, coma, spastic paralysis. High rate of permanent neurological sequelae.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Supportive care. Inactivated or live attenuated vaccines are highly effective for prevention.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Enveloped, spherical, flavivirus; positive-sense ssRNA. Four serotypes (DEN-1 to DEN-4).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Cultivated in mosquito cell lines or suckling mice.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to heat, lipid solvents, and disinfectants.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Vector: Aedes aegypti/albopictus mosquito. Primary infection induces immunity. Secondary infection with a different serotype leads to Antibody-Dependent Enhancement (ADE) -> severe disease.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Dengue fever (breakbone fever: high fever, severe joint/muscle pain, retro-orbital pain, rash). Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) / Dengue Shock Syndrome (DSS) due to vascular permeability.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Supportive fluid therapy. Vector control. Avoid aspirin (risk of bleeding).

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Encapsulated, round or oval yeast cell; reproduces by single budding. Surrounded by a very thick, prominent polysaccharide capsule.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Sabouraud's dextrose agar at 25°C or 37°C; forms cream-colored, mucoid yeast-like colonies.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Highly resistant in dry pigeon droppings, which serve as the primary environmental reservoir.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Inhalation of yeast cells. Polysaccharide capsule is highly anti-phagocytic. Melanizing enzyme protects against oxidative damage.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Cryptococcal meningitis (subacute/chronic meningitis with headache, neck stiffness, cranial nerve palsies, highly common in AIDS patients), pulmonary cryptococcosis.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Negative ink stain of CSF for rapid diagnosis. Combination of Amphotericin B and Flucytosine, followed by long-term Fluconazole. No vaccine.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Oval budding yeast cells, forms pseudohyphae (in tissue invasion) and thick-walled double-contoured chlamydospores on cornmeal agar.

details.title: Culture
details.content: Sabouraud's agar at 37°C; forms smooth, white-to-cream, yeast-scented colonies in 24-48 hours.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Moderate; sensitive to standard antifungals and heat.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Opportunistic pathogen (part of normal flora). Switches from yeast to pseudohyphae form during tissue invasion, adhering via cell surface proteins.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Candidiasis: Superficial thrush (oral pseudomembranous plaques), vulvovaginitis (cottage-cheese discharge, itching), cutaneous intertrigo. Systemic candidiasis (endocarditis, meningitis, multi-organ abscesses in neutropenic/catheterized patients).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Gram stain of scrapings. Topical or oral Nystatin/Clotrimazole for superficial infections; Fluconazole or Caspofungin/Amphotericin B for systemic candidiasis.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Sporozoans; intra-erythrocytic stages include ring forms (small, delicate, double chromatin dots), banana-shaped gametocytes (highly diagnostic).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Maintained in specialized erythrocyte cultures (in vitro) but not cultivated on standard agar.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Sensitive to antimalarial drugs, though drug-resistant strains (chloroquine-resistant) are highly prevalent.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Vector: female Anopheles mosquito. Infects RBCs, causing them to express sticky proteins (PfEMP-1) -> adherence to capillary endothelium -> microvascular occlusion.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Malaria (malignant tertian malaria): irregular cycles of high fever, shaking chills, profuse sweating, anemia, splenomegaly. Cerebral malaria (coma, death) due to microvascular occlusion.

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Thick/thin blood smear stained with Giemsa. Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs), Chloroquine, Primaquine. Mosquito control, bed nets.

details.title: Morphology
details.content: Amoeba. Two stages: Trophozoite (10-40 μm, motile, active, typically contains ingested RBCs) and Cyst (10-20 μm, dormant, spherical, 1-4 nuclei, chromatoid bodies).

details.title: Culture
details.content: Can be cultured in specialized monoxenic/axenic liquid media.

details.title: Resistance
details.content: Trophozoites are fragile and die in environment. Cysts are highly resistant, surviving chlorination and gastric acid.

details.title: Pathogenesis
details.content: Fecal-oral route (ingesting cysts). Excystation in ileum -> trophozoites invade colonic mucosa using histolytic enzymes -> flask-shaped ulcers. Can enter blood to liver.

details.title: Clinical Findings
details.content: Amoebic dysentery (abdominal pain, flatulence, bloody stools with mucus but little pus). Extra-intestinal: Amoebic liver abscess (jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, chocolate/anchovy-paste pus).

details.title: Treatment & Prevention
details.content: Saline smear (trophozoites) or iodine stain (cysts) of stool. Metronidazole (targets trophozoites) followed by paromomycin/diiodoquin (luminal amebicides for cysts).
